name: Merodach-Baladan
title: King of Babylon
summary: Merodach-Baladan (also known as Berodach-Baladan) was a Chaldean king of Babylon who sent envoys with letters and gifts to King Hezekiah of Judah after his illness. The visit became a test for Hezekiah, who showed the Babylonians all his treasures, leading the prophet Isaiah to warn of the coming Babylonian conquest.

keyEvents.title: Sends Envoys to Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: Merodach-Baladan sent a letter and a gift to King Hezekiah after hearing about his illness and recovery. This visit likely also had political motives, as Babylon sought allies against Assyria.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah Shows His Treasures
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah received the Babylonian envoys and proudly showed them all his treasuries, armories, and everything of value throughout his kingdom. There was nothing in his house or realm that he did not show them.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah Questions Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah came to Hezekiah and asked who these men were and where they had come from. Hezekiah told him that they came from the distant land of Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Judgment and Prophecy
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesied that all that Hezekiah had shown the Babylonians would one day be carried off to Babylon, and that some of his descendants would be taken as eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's Reaction to the Prophecy
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah replied that the Lord's word was good, and thought that there would at least be peace and security during his lifetime. His response reveals a mixture of humility and relief.
